articles.title: Inkling 2 Mini
articles.raw_description: Inkling 2 Mini is an open-weights model small enough to run on your laptop. It loops its middle layers to reason more per token and reach answers in fewer tokens. Try on Tinker Hugging Face Model card Today we are releasing Inkling 2 Mini, a fast, powerful model that’s small enough to run on your laptop. Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality. Inkling 2 Mini leads every open-weights model with less than 100B total parameters on benchmarks such as DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%). It runs faster than similarly performing models as well. articles.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
articles.raw_description: A language model is trained once and frozen. Making it better takes another training run, or a prompt, a harness or extra computation at inference that is gone once the task ends. We show a third way: to our knowledge for the first time, a language model rewrites its own weights by its own reasoning and becomes better, with no gradients and no training. We call this self-rewriting: the model is its own optimizer. In earlier work, a frontier model edited a much smaller one; here an open 27B model, given its weights, its graded answers and the ability to run itself, diagnoses its own failure and rewrites the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on problems it never saw. It keeps getting better: it tests its edits on practice problems and submits only what works, each edit improving on the last, and over eight consecutive sessions its accuracy only rises. It repairs a damaged copy of itself, like a broken robot that fixes itself without being rebuilt: the copy solves almost nothing, yet with no retraining and without ever reading the original weights, the model brings it back to over 80% of the original accuracy on image tasks it never saw. And the ability emerges with scale: in one model family, the smaller models make no edit or break themselves, and only the largest improves and repairs itself. articles.title: We promoted developers into architects without informing them
articles.raw_description: If you hate vibe coding, it’s because you’re still trying to do the old job. AI does what you ask and won’t push back on requirements that slows your app or delete tables you created for testing. Be an architect instead of developer. All posts We promoted developers into architects without informing them Mani Doraisamy 8 hours ago 3 1 Yesterday, I was debugging a performance problem with our Google Forms addon. It turned out my colleague had vibe coded the logging part, so that he could monitor the new installs every week. Monitoring new customers is the most important part of running a business, so he is absolutely right in doing that. Except, he was logging the user’s email and Google has severely restricted how much detail you can get about the user since last December. So, AI had written a series of try/catch statements: First, try to get the email if the user gave consent to share it during installation. If it fails, it would try to fetch his user ID. If that fails, it would log an error saying the user has installed, but we don’t know his email or user ID. All of these are one line of code, but internally each of these makes multiple API calls to Google servers. Since logging was the first line to execute after installation, the welcome screen took 15 seconds to load. What is the right code for this? articles.title: Valkey kills the skiplist, cuts sorted set overhead by up to 43%
articles.raw_description: How Valkey 9.2 replaces the skiplist used by large sorted sets with a cache-friendly B+ tree, reducing memory overhead while improving several ordered-set operations. From Skiplists to B+ Trees: Making Valkey Sorted Sets More Memory Efficient Technical Deep Dive 2026-11-16 · Rain Valentine , Dragos Andriciuc A sorted set can spend more memory describing how its elements are ordered than storing the elements themselves. In Valkey 9.2 that changes: the skiplist is replaced by a high-fanout B+ tree variant called fbtree . fbtree combines the high fanout and contiguous storage of a conventional B+ tree with several optimizations designed for Valkey's workload and memory allocator, including feature-based lookups, SIMD searches, linked leaves, and fast paths for sequential inserts and pops. In a 5-million-member test, it reduced per-member memory overhead by 36–43%, saving up to 109 MB. Let's take a look at why this change happened and how it works. Why replace the skiplist? Large sorted sets that exceed the listpack threshold are backed by a skiplist paired with a hashtable (smaller sorted sets use a compact listpack representation that stores elements sequentially in contiguous memory). The hashtable gives O(1) lookups by member, while the skiplist gives O(log n) ordered lookups by rank or score. articles.title: 「Windows Server 2028」で「WSUS」や「SMB 1.0」、「VBScript」などが削除へ／「Windows PowerShell 5.1」「WDS」は非推奨に、レガシーBIOSでの起動も不可
articles.raw_description: 先日パブリックプレビューが始まった次期サーバーOS「Windows Server 2028」には、削除・非推奨となる機能がある。米Microsoftが自社のドキュメントサイトで明らかにしている。 ニュース 「Windows Server 2028」で「WSUS」や「SMB 1.0」、「VBScript」などが削除へ 「Windows PowerShell 5.1」「WDS」は非推奨に、レガシーBIOSでの起動も不可 樽井 秀人 2026年11月20日 19:05 「Microsoft Learn」のドキュメント「Features removed or no longer developed in Windows Server」 先日パブリックプレビューが始まった 次期サーバーOS「Windows Server 2028」には、削除・非推奨となる機能がある。米Microsoftが自社のドキュメントサイトで明らかにしている。 削除される機能 「Windows Server 2028」で削除される主な機能は、以下の通り。 「WINS」（Windows Internet Name Service） サーバーの用途：DNSベースの名前解決へ移行 「DirectAccess」 ：「Always On VPN」へ移行 PPTP/L2TPプロトコル によるリモートアクセス：IKEv2またはSSTPへ移行 「SMB 1.0」 ：「SMB 2.0/3.0」へ移行 「VBScript」 ：管理スクリプトは「PowerShell」、Webのスクリプトは「JavaScript」へ移行 「WMIC」（Windows Management Instrumentation Command-line）ユーティリティ ：WMI自体は削除されない。「PowerShell」やプログラムからのWMIクエリへ置き換え 「Windows Server Update Services」（WSUS） サーバーの用途 PC/AT（PCAT）とレガシーBIOSによる起動：UEFIが必須に。「Hyper-V」でWindows Server 2028を動かすゲストVMも第2世代が必要。旧OSを動かす第1世代VMのサポートには影響しない 「MultiPoint Services」：「リモート デスクトップ サービス」へ移行 「Shielded VMs」：要件を満たす場合は「Trusted VMs」へ移行（ただし、プレビュー段階の「Trusted VMs」はフェイルオーバークラスターや「Hyper-V レプリカ」に未対応） 「AT Time Service」（ATSVC）と「at.exe」：「schtasks」を利用 「.NET Framework 3.5」 のオプションコンポーネント：スタンドアロンインストーラーでは引き続き入手可能 影響が大きそうなのはWSUSだ。ただし、削除は「Windows Server 2028」に限られ、「Windows Server 2025」など旧版では各製品のサポート期間中、引き続き利用できる。Microsoftは、閉域網などでの更新管理についても今後情報を共有するとしている。 非推奨となる機能 また、以下の機能は「Windows Server 2028」から非推奨となる。非推奨の機能は引き続き製品に含まれ、本番環境での利用もサポートされるが、新機能の開発は行われない。将来のリリースで削除される可能性もあるため、できるだけ早く後継製品や代替製品への移行を計画しておきたい。
